Title: Earnings call transcript: Toyota Industries Q2 2025 faces EPS miss, revenue up By Investing.com
How to position for the next wave of AI-led scientific breakthroughs. Investing.com’s stocks of the week. # Earnings call transcript: Toyota Industries Q2 2025 faces EPS miss, revenue up. Toyota Industries Corporation reported its Q2 2025 earnings, revealing a striking earnings per share (EPS) miss but exceeding revenue forecasts. Despite the EPS shortfall, the stock experienced a modest increase of 0.62%, reflecting a complex investor sentiment. According to InvestingPro data, the company has maintained profitability over the last twelve months with a basic EPS of 4.61 USD. Toyota Industries demonstrated resilience in its Q2 2025 performance, despite an EPS of -37.69 against a forecast of 94.58. The company achieved a revenue of ¥2,058.6 billion, marking a ¥43.2 billion year-over-year increase. This revenue growth, coupled with strategic expansions, helped maintain a stable market position amidst global economic challenges. The company’s EPS of -37.69 was significantly below the forecasted 94.58, resulting in a negative surprise of -139.85. However, revenue exceeded expectations, coming in at ¥1,068.14 trillion versus the forecasted ¥994.67 billion, a 7.39% surprise. Following the earnings release, Toyota Industries’ stock rose by 0.62%, closing at ¥16,825. This increase, despite the EPS miss, suggests investor confidence driven by revenue growth and strategic initiatives. Toyota revised its full-year operating profit forecast to ¥100 billion, acknowledging ongoing challenges in key markets. The company anticipates continued economic uncertainty in North America and Europe, with expected impacts from US tariffs on its industrial vehicle segment. "We are experiencing uncertainty in the North American market," a high-level executive noted, emphasizing the need for strategic adjustments. An accounting department manager highlighted, "Engine certification related costs total ¥73.7 billion," pointing to ongoing financial impacts.
